summary:
Team Summary – LUNA MARS

We are a passionate team of young innovators participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our team combines skills in research, data analysis, programming, and web development to solve real-world space exploration challenges.

Through our project, LUNA MARS, we aim to connect Earth-based scientific research with future Moon and Mars exploration by identifying and comparing terrestrial analog sites using scientific data and interactive visualizations.

Our mission is to make planetary exploration research more accessible, understandable, and useful for future space missions.
details:
Project Details – LUNA MARS | Earth Analog Finder

LUNA MARS is an interactive, data-driven platform designed to identify and compare locations on Earth that share geological and environmental characteristics with the Moon and Mars.

Our project addresses a major challenge in space exploration: selecting suitable Earth-based locations to test technologies, train astronauts, and prepare for future lunar and Martian missions.

The platform combines interactive maps, planetary comparisons, heatmaps, and a customizable similarity-scoring system. Users can select a lunar or Martian target, explore terrestrial analog sites, adjust the importance of environmental factors such as temperature, solar exposure, ice availability, and terrain slope, and compare locations based on their research objectives.

The project also connects analog environments with potential testing applications, helping researchers explore which locations may be useful for rover mobility, scientific instruments, and exploration operations.

Tools and Technologies: We developed the interactive web platform using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, incorporating mapping, data visualization, and quantitative comparison techniques. Our research draws on publicly available scientific information and datasets from NASA and other scientific institutions.

Innovation: What makes LUNA MARS creative is its combination of planetary analog research, transparent scoring methods, interactive geographic visualization, and mission-oriented recommendations in one accessible platform. Rather than presenting a static list of locations, it allows users to explore how different scientific priorities affect site rankings.

Throughout development, we considered geological relevance, environmental conditions, data availability, scientific uncertainty, usability, and the practical requirements of future exploration missions. Preliminary estimates are distinguished from verified measurements to avoid presenting model-generated similarity scores as official scientific findings.

Our intended impact is to make planetary analog research more accessible, support evidence-informed planning for Earth-based mission simulations, and provide a foundation for future research using additional satellite observations and verified environmental datasets.

Ultimately, LUNA MARS aims to help bridge the gap between studying environments on Earth and preparing humanity to explore the Moon and Mars.
